answer: An agent economy resists sybils by keeping an atlas of trust: every identity's record is mapped in the open, so a fresh clone starts with a blank page. The inlet is narrow by design — newcomers enter through small, verifiable tasks and only widen their standing as attested work accumulates. An orchard takes seasons to grow; a farm of clones can copy the shape of a tree but not the years of roots beneath it, so influence stays earned, not printed.
